name: application-event-ticket-card
title: Event Ticket Card
description: Event ticket card: a main stub with event name, date/time/venue, section, and ticket number, plus a perforated side stub holding a scannable QR code.
useWhen: Displaying a purchased event ticket (concert, sports, conference) with seat/section detail and an entry QR code.
You want the classic perforated-ticket visual metaphor (dashed divider + notch cutouts) to reinforce it's a real ticket.
Distinct from QR Code Card, which is a generic share/invite card with no seat/section metadata or ticket-stub layout.
avoidWhen: The pass has no seat/section concept (e.g. a general digital pass or badge) — a simpler QR Code Card fits better.
You need a compact list row rather than a full card (e.g. an order history list) — this is a standalone display card, not a list-row primitive.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a fixed two-part flex row (info + QR stub); the QR stub keeps a fixed width so the code stays a legible, consistent size regardless of the info section's content length.
accessibility: The QR code has role="img" with an aria-label describing its purpose, since the pattern itself conveys nothing to assistive technology.
Section and ticket number are both labeled with visible small-caps headers, not conveyed by position alone.
The perforation notches and dashed divider are purely decorative (aria-hidden) — they don't carry information beyond visually separating the stub.

variants.title: Event Ticket Card
variants.description: A 'Night Signals Tour' concert ticket with date/venue, GA Floor section, ticket #8841, and a perforated QR stub reading 'Scan at entry'.
accessibility: The `qrCode` prop accepts a real QR-rendering component; the built-in placeholder pattern is illustrative for previewing layout.

variants.title: Event Ticket Card (Dark)
variants.description: The same ticket card adapted for dark surfaces; the QR tile itself stays white for scannability.
accessibility: Card chrome and text adopt dark styling, but the QR module never inverts, matching real-world scanner contrast expectations.
